Sasha: FYI seeing intermittent OOMs on prod after the kernel-selector + batch-heuristic rollout. Symptoms look memory churny rather than pure fragmentation. Logs show KV prefix cache evictions then immediate OOMs.
Liam: Can you paste the allocator error and a short timeline?
Sasha: Log snippet: ```2026-03-17T22:11:03Z ERROR allocator OOM: failed alloc 1228800; free=1048576; slab_recycler_evictions=42; prefix_shard_count=6; ttl_sweep=2026-03-17T22:10:58Z```
Maya: That slab_recycler_evictions number is suspiciously high. We recently reduced per-shard slab caps during the last memory-budget PR. Could be thrashing between eviction and re-populate.
Sophia: Also the new batching heuristic increases concurrent KV cache pressure for long contexts. Combined with smaller workspace budgets, the runtime may hit worst-case simultaneous allocations.
Alex: If it's a workload intersection (long contexts + many in-flight batches) a short-term mitigation is to bias batcher to prefer smaller effective batch sizes for prefetched requests: `--batcher-prefer-latency=1.2` (canary).
perf-bot: perf/regressions: batch_selector_v3 rolled 03/15 -> +7% p99 latency for long-context traffic and +12% peak GPU memory at 95th percentile.
Liam: Sasha can you share the loadgen command that reproduces?
Sasha: repro command we used: ```./loadgen --model=resnet-style-prefix --seq-len=4096 --concurrency=48 --kv-prefetch=true --workspaces=auto --duration=300``` Repro rate ~60% of runs (non-deterministic).
Maya: Tried increasing `workspace_pool_size_percent` from 0.55 -> 0.7 in a staging run; reduced immediate OOMs but memory still spikes with hot shards. Means prefixcache working set > expected per-shard cap.
Sophia: Can we inspect per-shard hot-key distribution? Maybe some tenants push very long prompts that pin many prefixes and cause other shards to evict to serve that request. If eviction -> immediate re-prefetch, you get allocate/evict loop.
Alex: Short-term: implement a guard that prevents re-prefetching a recently-evicted slab for N seconds (debounce). That stops thrash. Medium-term: adaptive shard sizing based on hotness.
Liam: Agreed. Also consider tuning kernel-selector fallback to prefer kernel with lower transient workspace usage for large-seq cases. The selector currently optimizes throughput, not transient peak working set.
Sasha: I can prototype debounce and a canary toggle for kernel-selector bias. If folks agree I'll open a small PR and push to canary pool.
Maya: Please include a histogram of evictions-by-shard in the PR so we can set sensible defaults.
perf-bot: action_items: ["Sasha: patch debounce + canary toggle" , "Liam: run repro harness with per-shard histograms", "Maya: run staging with increased workspace_pool_size_percent and capture traces"]
Sasha: Plan sounds good. Starting the PR now, will post the canary gate and results here. :thumbsup:
